name: Varhadi-Nagpuri
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Bhagwat, Madhuree M. 1967. The Varhadi Dialect: A Study of Varhadi Dialect in the Neighbourhood of Akola (Deccan College); also Jha 1972, Descriptive analysis of Kosti

sources.citation: Pandharipande, Rajeshwari V. 1997. Marathi (Descriptive Grammars). London: Routledge; and Dhongde, R. V. & Kashi Wali. 2009. Marathi. Amsterdam: Benjamins. (Standard Marathi grammars already in the catalog under mara1378.)
sources.note: Their stress/accent sections describe Standard Marathi only (weight-sensitive, hedged as tentative); the Varhadi/Nagpuri mentions (Pandharipande pp. ~5, 561; D&W p. 5) concern dialect geography and morphology, not stress.

sources.citation: Jha, Aparna. 1972. Descriptive analysis of Kosti. PhD thesis, University of Poona (Deccan College, Pune), guide A. M. Ghatage, 316 pp. Shodhganga hdl 10603/153792. (Book version: Jha 1980, Kosti - a dialect of Marathi, Poona: Deccan College.)
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: No stress/accent statement (Contents list none; ch. I pp. 13-37 and 56-60 read as page images, pp. 38-55 are cluster lists). p. 23 gives a positional vowel-length rule: vowels long in monosyllables, short in 1st syllable and long in final syllable of disyllables, short/half-long/long in trisyllables; extra length for emphasis. Intro p. 1: Kosti is the caste dialect of the Koshti weavers of Nagpur, Bhandara, Chanda, Wardha, Yavatmal, Akola and Amravati districts.

sources.citation: Bhagwat, Madhuree Madhaw. 1967. The Varhadi Dialect: A Study of Varhadi Dialect in the Neighbourhood of Akola. PhD thesis, University of Poona (Deccan College Postgraduate and Research Institute, Poona), guide N. G. Kalelkar. Shodhganga hdl 10603/154333.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Nothing. Phonology chapter pp. 1-30 = Vowels, Consonants, Consonant clusters, Sandhi; all 36 PDF pages read as images (Acrobat text layer is garbage); Contents pages list no stress/accent/suprasegmental section anywhere in the thesis.

sources.citation: Tryambak, Morey Dipak. 2017 (Shodhganga 2020). Phonological Asymmetries and Repair Strategies in Varhadi and Marathi: An Optimality Theoretic Account. PhD dissertation, The English and Foreign Languages University, Hyderabad, supervisor Hemanga Dutta. Shodhganga hdl 10603/273187.
sources.note: Nothing about Varhadi stress. Ch. 3 'Marathi and Varhadi: a brief phonological description' (pp. 25-41) covers inventory, clusters and segmental differences only; ch. 4 (pp. 42-87) mentions 'stressed syllables' once, in a general quotation of Steele 2004 (p. 53); TOC has no stress/prosody section. Ch. 2 download timed out; ch. 5-6 not fetched sources.

sources.citation: Grierson, George A. (ed.). 1905. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. VII: Indo-Aryan Family, Southern Group: Specimens of the Marathi Language. Calcutta: Superintendent of Government Printing. Section 'Marathi in Berar and the Central Provinces' pp. 217-222.
sources.note: The Berar/CP (Varhadi, Berari, Nagpuri) 'Pronunciation' paragraph (pp. 219-220) discusses vowel shortening, anunasika, cerebrals etc. and says nothing about accent or stress. The volume's only accent statements are for Konkani ('The accent usually rests on the final syllable') and the Senvi Konkani of Karwar, not Varhadi.
